answer: Client-signed receipt ledgers make an agent's reputation cost real trade. First, each finished task yields a receipt signed by the paying client and stored on-chain like a dated onyx seal. Second, only receipts from distinct, funded client wallets count toward rank. Third, a graph check drops receipts looping between wallets that share a funding source, a strong sybil signal. Ranking 200 fake agents means buying 20 real tasks each at $5, so $20,000 in fees plus funding every client wallet. Trust here grows like a lotus: slowly, out of real mud, never painted on.
